articles.description: British multinational aerospace, arms and information security company BAE Systems is to cut more than 1,000 jobs in its air division.

articles.title: Kemi and Andy put another nail in the coffin of his consensus politics | John Crace
articles.description: The Tory leader is hardwired for conflict. It was futile for the PM to demand an end to her patronising tone Well, that didn’t take long. When Andy Burnham first arrived in No 10, he said he was determined to do things differently. He wanted a new, consensual politics where he would work with other parties to put the country back together. Safe to say, that dream is already dead in the water. At least when it comes to his exchanges with Kemi Badenoch at prime minister’s questions. Andy might go through the motions of promising Ed Davey and various backbenchers a veneer of cross-party support that may or may not become reality – even Andy doesn’t have a clue which is which – but when it comes to Kemi, it’s now just a bloodless slanging match. Bloodless because there’s nothing really at stake. It’s all just a performance. Kemi has yet to land a blow on Burnham, so both leaders are merely playing to a gallery of their own backbenchers. Continue reading...

articles.title: The Quechua rapper and an artistic movement reclaiming language of the Incas
articles.description: Renata Flores has gained global recognition for her music in Indigenous language whose speakers have faced social stigma With her long black hair braided into beaded plaits, a delicate silver nose ring, and intricately patterned Andean textile draped around her chest above baggy, low-riding jeans, Renata Flores is a visual reflection of her music: a fusion of traditional and transgressive, old and new, rural and urban. Nicknamed the “queen of Quechua rap”, Flores, 25, has earned global recognition for mixing Peru’s main Indigenous language and Andean instruments with the urban beats of trap, rap, hip-hop and reggaeton. Continue reading...

articles.title: The reboot of poor Jensen Huang almost worked. But who can explain away 30 leather jackets? | Emma Brockes
articles.description: He seemed like the thinking person’s tech titan. But then came the affairs, the share collapse – and of course, the sorry items in his wardrobe A few years ago, I attended a small dinner at a friend’s house in the US at which a tech billionaire was the guest of honour. He wasn’t one of the most famous tech billionaires – I’d never heard of him, although I used his communications platform every day. Nonetheless, it was exciting to get up close to someone that staggeringly rich to see if he was different from the rest of us. And he was different, sort of. Leaning back in his chair, he seemed to suggest, in a bored kind of way, that in the event of a US standoff with Russia, Putin nuking London would be the sort of collateral damage Washington could tolerate. A bit of an odd thing to say to a stranger. He didn’t observe the usual rules of conversation but rather, like a Roman emperor waiting to be entertained, remained belligerently aloof. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: UK ministers reportedly ask Google to block Russell Brand’s YouTube account
articles.description: Government makes request to tech firm in wake of 51-year-old’s prison message, according to Sky News The British government has reportedly asked Google to deactivate Russell Brand ’s YouTube account after he was able to publish a message claiming his innocence following his conviction for rape and sexual assault. A justice minister met representatives of the technology company to make the request after social media firm Meta disabled the former comedian’s profiles on Instagram and Facebook, according to Sky News . Continue reading...

articles.title: Ex-Tory MPs barred from shaping Reform UK’s immigration policy, says Zia Yusuf
articles.description: Comments by Reform’s home affairs spokesperson raise questions about unity at top of the party Former Conservative defectors to Reform UK have been barred from shaping the party’s immigration policy, its home affairs spokesperson has claimed, excluding in effect the majority of the party’s MPs. “If you are in the category of being concerned about [former Conservatives being involved in Reform], none of the above are going to be involved in immigration policy or borders policy,” Zia Yusuf told a podcast by the Spectator magazine. Continue reading...

articles.title: Xi Jinping rallies against protectionism as he welcomes Trump to Apec summit
articles.description: Chinese president greets US counterpart with rare hug before blockbuster trilateral meeting with Putin China’s Xi Jinping rallied Asia-Pacific nations against trade protectionism on Wednesday morning before heading to the airport to welcome Donald Trump, whose administration has just further restricted advanced chip exports, with a rare hug. The Chinese president spent Wednesday’s opening day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit switching lanes between multilateralist and big-power politics, culminating in a group photo where he stood central among fellow leaders. He was flanked by Trump and Vladimir Putin – whose blockbuster trilateral meeting will dominate Thursday’s proceedings as the summit gets to its business end. Continue reading...

articles.title: Traces of filler found in heart and brain of woman who died after ‘butt lift’, UK inquest hears
articles.description: Jury told Jordan Parke injected seven times amount of filler he was taught to use during Alice Webb’s cosmetic procedure A man known as the “Lip King” who carried out a “Brazilian butt lift” (BBL) on a woman who later died injected her with seven times the amount of filler that he had been taught to use, an inquest jury has been told. Traces of the filler that Jordan Parke injected into Alice Webb, 33, were discovered in her heart, lungs, brain and kidneys, the inquest heard. Continue reading...

articles.title: Shabana Mahmood backs ban on police marching in pride events in uniform
articles.description: Home secretary says ‘routine two-tier policing’ does not exist, but public trust in impartial law enforcement must be restored Shabana Mahmood has backed a ban on police officers marching in pride events in uniform as she said there had been a “few examples” of two-tier policing . Although she said there was no systematic or routine two-tier policing, the home secretary said “a new impartiality standard” was necessary to reverse the fall in the public’s faith in law enforcement. Continue reading...

articles.title: Bacterial toxin produced by E coli leading suspect in rise in bowel cancer among under-50s
articles.description: Scientists tell Commons exposure to colibactin in early life is potential driver of early-onset colorectal cancer Exposure to a bacterial toxin in early life has emerged as a leading suspect in the rise of bowel cancer among those under 50, MPs have heard. Cases of early-onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and while rising obesity and a fall in physical activity are contributors, researchers believe other factors must also be involved. Continue reading...

articles.title: Birmingham council granted interim ban on union jacks on lamp-posts
articles.description: High court judge issues order against Raise the Colours over flags on council-owned street furniture The campaign group Raise the Colours has been temporarily banned from placing union jacks on lamp-posts and roundabouts in Birmingham after a legal challenge by the local council. The high court judge Emma Kelly granted an interim injunction banning the placing of all flags on council-owned street furniture without prior permission in a judgment issued on Wednesday, Birmingham city council said. Continue reading...

articles.title: How Ukraine landed a blow to Putin’s prized bridge - The Latest
articles.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has hailed an ‘unprecedented operation’ to severely damage a critical bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea. The Kerch bridge was built by Russia after its illegal annexation of the Crimean peninsula in 2014, and the attack this week marks a significant blow to Vladimir Putin’s war efforts just before his meeting with the US and Chinese presidents. With Ukraine able to secure a significant military victory, have we reached a turning point in the conflict? Lucy Hough speaks to senior international correspondent Luke Harding and the author of Betrayal : Trump, Putin and the New Age of Conquest Continue reading...

articles.title: The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?
articles.description: No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook. The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash. Continue reading...

articles.title: Kelly Gough is simply astounding as Desire Under the Elms reaches the heights of Greek tragedy
articles.description: Almeida theatre, London Part-Phaedra and part-Medea, Gough is mesmerising in Ebenezer Bamgboye’s stylised staging of Eugene O’Neill’s family drama You would not know that Eugene O’Neill’s play was originally set on a mid 19th-century farm. This version by director Ebenezer Bamgboye brings modernity with its sleek storytelling, but also nods to the ancient Greek drama O’Neill was emulating in his 1924 play about illicit desire and the father-son fight for land. It makes for a strange mix at first, beguiling and bewildering in equal measure. Bamgboye employs some of the striking theatricality that he brought to his magnetic adaptation of The Lonely Londoners two years ago. It is an original refashioning, the script sharper with less of the exposition that might date it, but the directorial flourishes come so thick and fast that it is stylised to the bone. Bamgboye has previously worked with Rebecca Frecknall (who staged the leaden O’Neill drama A Moon for the Misbegotten last year) and the first half seems to pay too big a debt to her style of work. Continue reading...

articles.title: Instant gratification is ruining our lives – and for me it started with my CD player’s shuffle button | Adrian Chiles
articles.description: Not even a compelling TV drama can stop me from staring at my phone. But this urge started 40 years ago, with what was at first presented as a useful feature I blame the shuffle button. That’s what started me on the long road to a thoroughly scattered mind – generally unable to focus on anything for more than a few minutes or even seconds. I was always a bit like this, hence an ADHD diagnosis in later life. But back in the day I still managed to read a lot of books, watch long films and listen to whole records at one sitting. Now? Not so much. Actually, hardly ever. Even something on television that I’m really engaged in – a drama or a football match – can hold me for only a few minutes before I find myself scrolling on my phone looking for I know not what. I don’t know whether it’s because I’m drawn to the small phone screen, or rather that I find absorption with whatever I’m watching on the big flatscreen just too much to bear. Continue reading...

articles.title: Sublime and ridiculous, but I love the wild experiments of Huddersfield’s contemporary music festival
articles.description: The 49th edition of the new music festival begins this weekend. Where else can you indulge in a world of pure imagination, see the future – and chat over a curry with some of contemporary music’s biggest names? The Huddersfield contemporary music festival – or hcmf , with contemporary-cool lower-case, as it’s styled – celebrates its 49th edition this month, turning the darkness of late November into a beacon of blazing new-music ambition in West Yorkshire. It’s a festival with an extraordinary history. Nowhere else in the UK could you have bumped into Karlheinz Stockhausen and his entourage in a pub in the late 1980s; nowhere else could you have sat in the audience alongside Björk at the town hall; in no other town might you have stumbled on Pierre Boulez, John Cage, Olivier Messiaen and Yvonne Loriod chatting about the best place to have a curry that night. (Well, maybe I can’t guarantee the dinner discussion but all of the above have visited the festival over the past five decades.) Continue reading...

articles.title: Shame is the only punishment in Australian cricket’s sandpaper scandal | Geoff Lemon
articles.description: The time for formal measures has passed but all involved have betrayed the trust of a country whose Test team is sacred Cry havoc. But Cameron Bancroft did not let anything slip, not after close to a decade of keeping his mouth firmly shut. It was a deliberate, considered and lengthy deed of revelation that the former Test opening bat chose to publish in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday, claiming to finally fill in a wealth of detail around Australian cricket’s 2018 cheating scandal that so many others seem to have gone to such lengths to keep concealed. It was also a devastating repudiation of Pat Cummins, a teammate of equivalent juniority to Bancroft during their few months playing together, but now the Test captain, who had delivered his own manifesto in spoken form at a press conference last week. That version of events, in which Cummins was adamant that he had never been aware of any kind of ball-tampering in Australian colours, was what pushed Bancroft from silence to speech. “It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone,” Bancroft wrote. “What I saw, experienced and lived with not only him, but everyone else on that tour in South Africa is not the public account he g

articles.title: Alexander Zverev notified of abuse lawsuit by ex-partner during ATP Finals
articles.description: Men’s world No 1 allegedly violated terms of settlement Lawyers say Zverev will ‘defend himself against lawsuit’ Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday. The latest legal case against the men’s world No 1 brought by the mother of the former couple’s daughter alleges that Zverev violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her. The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with the French sports daily L’Equipe earlier this year that “it has been proven that the accusations were false” and “my innocence has been proven”. Continue reading...

articles.title: Rugby brain injury lawsuits again on brink of collapse over medical documents delay
articles.description: Claimants’ legal team argues for extension until January Future of case rests on decisions of the two judges After six years of interminable and expensive legal argument , the two lawsuits involving hundreds of brain-damaged rugby players appear to be on the brink of collapsing. The lead counsel representing the players, Paul Downes KC, had conceded in June that the claimants were in the “last-chance saloon” after repeatedly missing court-mandated deadlines for the disclosure of documents to the defendants. Having done so again this October, they now appear to be somewhere out beyond it. Continue reading...

articles.title: Leicester part ways with BC Game after sponsor’s partnership with porn actor
articles.description: Cryptocurrency casino made Eva Elfie a brand ambassador Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’ Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK , had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024. This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”. Continue reading...

articles.title: Reid Wiseman, the astronaut shooting for the moon in F1 with Mercedes
articles.description: Nasa crew member is fast seeing the similarities between flying Artemis II into lunar orbit and the F1 team’s drive for sporting brilliance There are characters aplenty within Formula One, a sport that attracts the larger‑than-life, and at the sharp end it can be a parade ground for swaggering egos. Yet the newest addition to the paddock is a man whose quietly spoken, understated thoughtfulness and insight are compelling. Now part of the Mercedes team, Reid Wiseman has been to the moon and with it brings a perspective like no other. Wiseman was one of four astronauts, alongside Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen, who completed the Artemis II lunar flyby in April. Last month Wiseman, the mission’s commander, became an ambassador for Mercedes’ F1 team, formalising a relationship that had been growing over several years, to the delight of his daughter, Katey, a fan of the newly crowned world champion, Kimi Antonelli. Continue reading...

articles.title: PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI
articles.description: Disruption comes at critical moment, with Grand Theft Auto VI one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in history PlayStation has suffered widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in recent gaming history. The disruption emerged Wednesday, causing frustrated players to flood social media with complaints about failed logins and server connection problems downloading games and updates. Continue reading...

articles.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
articles.description: Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area. Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street . Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed. Continue reading...

articles.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% after petrol and diesel prices hit record high
articles.description: Increase in October piles pressure on households as Iran war pushes up oil cost and rattles global economy Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% to £2,166 from January Inflation in the UK rose to 3.6% in October after petrol prices increased and diesel hit a record high amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East. Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) show the headline rate of inflation as measured by the consumer prices index rose from 3.5% in September and was in line with City economists’ forecasts. Continue reading...

articles.title: Democrats demand answers from Howard Lutnick about Nvidia and his family’s business
articles.description: Democratic lawmakers ask if commerce secretary favored Nvidia to enrich his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald The US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, faces mounting questions over his handling of the Nvidia affair as Democratic lawmakers demand answers over his family firm’s vast stake in the tech company. Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Lutnick ran for decades before joining the Trump administration , held shares in Nvidia worth “hundreds of millions of dollars” while Lutnick made key decisions affecting the tech firm’s ability to operate, according to Democrats on three key congressional committees. Continue reading...

articles.title: Madden review – Nicolas Cage is a cartoonish NFL legend in David O Russell’s stinker
articles.description: Oscar-nominated director delivers a thoroughly unserious biopic, wasting Christian Bale and Sienna Miller’s talents John Madden was a beloved American original, the burly football coach who segued easily from Super Bowl burnout to television darling to the last name in gaming as the NFL was overtaking baseball as the national pastime. When he wasn’t crashing into family rooms on football Sundays and Thanksgivings to break down the game’s rough complexities into fun-sized morsels, he was pressing flesh with everyday Americans while barnstorming the country in his Madden cruiser – the coach bus he depended on to compensate for his well-documented fear of flying. That the Madden video game franchise outlived the avuncular Minnesotan , whose death at age 85 in 2021 was mourned throughout the sport, is as much a testament to his singular knack for teaching the game’s fundaments as it is to his willingness to bring his classroom to students, wherever they might huddle. But Madden, a new Amazon biopic that can’t decide whether it’s serious or slapstick, has drawn all the wrong lessons. Continue reading...

articles.title: Theodore Zeldin obituary
articles.description: Revered historian, author and francophile with a novelistic approach to his subject On the website the Oxford Muse , which the francophile Oxford historian Theodore Zeldin set up in 2001 to bring strangers together for mutually liberating conversations, there is a little section on dancing. “Few realise,” he wrote, “how important a part dancing has played in the history of freedom.” During the French Revolution, 700 dance halls opened; in the 1830s, socialists liked dancing the galop because it involved changing partners; in 1968 (or thereabouts) women stopped letting men take the lead. “Dancing is like a carnival, freeing you from what you normally are,” Zeldin wrote. “Dancing together creates harmonies between people with different tastes. That is also what conversation seeks.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Am I Caribbean, or am I a tourist? How art helped me find the answer
articles.description: During my visit to the Fuze Caribbean art fair in the Bahamas, I marvelled at how creators captured the complex nature of Caribbeanness Don’t get The Long Wave delivered to your inbox? Sign up here When I tell people I’m travelling to the Bahamas to report on Fuze Caribbean art fair, no one believes I’m really going for work. There are smirks and jokes about it being a tough life, about drinking from coconuts on the beach. The tourist gaze pervades global perceptions of the Caribbean. This week, I speak to the region’s artists about how they use images to speak back. I have Antiguan and Jamaican heritage, so I’m familiar with the fantasies the Caribbean sparks, which Antiguan-American writer Jamaica Kincaid described as so beautiful that its fluffy white clouds, blue spectral waters and “bottomless” black nights seemed “unreal”. Images have done much to flatten the Caribbean in the global imagination – so why shouldn’t Caribbean people use images to speak back? Continue reading...

articles.title: The Papers: 'I'd rejoin the Army to fight Russia' and 'Boiling point'

articles.title: Anthropic sets share price at $83 for stock market debut, above expected range
articles.description: Artificial intelligence firm positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, with trading slated to begin Thursday Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83 on Wednesday, positioning the artificial intelligence company for one of the biggest initial public offerings in history. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange. The pricing is above Anthropic’s earlier estimates. Last week, the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set its preliminary share price at $70 to $78. With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) from $1.26tn to $1.41tn. articles.description: Ken Griffin Disposes NYC Condo For $58 Million After Socialist Mamdani's "Creepy & Weird" Video Citadel founder Ken Griffin has reportedly sold his duplex at Manhattan's 740 Park Avenue to New York Jets owner Woody Johnson for $58 million, according to Bloomberg . Griffin saw the writing on the wall earlier this year when reformist socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani vilified him in a creepy socialist propaganda video promoting a new pied-à-terre tax. The report said Griffin sold the property for about $13 million above the roughly $45 million he paid, representing a 29% increase before taxes and transaction costs . Earlier this year, at the Milken Institute Global Conference, Griffin explained, " What the mayor of New York has made clear to my partners, and principally my New York partners, is that we need to double down on our bet in Miami ." "Looking at what Mamdani did to me and, more broadly, is doing to the city of New York is triggering the trauma I went through in Chicago," Griffin said at the time. articles.description: Neocon Fox News Host Goes Mask-Off With Stunning Attack On JD Vance Fox News host Brian Kilmeade let his neoconservative mask slip, launching a blistering attack on Vice President JD Vance over his opposition to another prolonged war in the Middle East. The longtime Fox & Friends co-host used his radio show to declare that Vance never should have made it to the vice presidency, apparently taking exception to the vice president's longstanding skepticism of Washington's military adventures in the Middle East. "I had to play this. It is so aggravating," Kilmeade complained after airing clips from Vance's interview with fellow Fox News host Laura Ingraham. "There is not one person that I have ever met that wants an endless war, who will say the president's got to keep fighting no matter what." Kilmeade then offered his preferred strategy, which was heavy on the usual military jargon, but noticeably short on specifics. "Win, neutralize our 40-year enemy, and you end it when you want to end it," he said, before launching a surprising attack on the vice president. articles.title: Average 20Y Auction Prices On The Screws
articles.description: Average 20Y Auction Prices On The Screws Unlike last week's debacle of a Treasury auction week, which saw some real stinkers including a catastrophic 10Y auction, moments ago the Treasury sold $42BN in 20Y paper in a perfectly average auction.  The week's lone coupon auction priced at a high yield of 5.459%, down 1bp from October's 5.469% and on the screws with the When Issued. The bid to cover was 2.63, down from 2.73 but right on top of the six-auction average which was also 2.63. The internals were solid, with Indirects rising to tp 60.185% from 58.156%, and the highest since August, if below the 6-auction average of 63.6%. And with Directs taking 26.7%, also in line with the recent average of 24.3%, Dealers were left holding 13.1%, a perfectly average number and just 1% above the recent average of 12.0%. Overall, this was a perfectly average (and forgettable) 20Y auction, although with yields sliding to session lows as the 10Y trades down to a yield of 5.05%, that is hardly bad news in a market that remains extremely on edge.  Tyler Durden Wed, 11/18/2026 - 13:23

articles.title: Destroyer Deployments Will Stretch To Nearly A Year, Navy Chief Tells Stunned Military Families
articles.description: Destroyer Deployments Will Stretch To Nearly A Year, Navy Chief Tells Stunned Military Families The USS Abraham Lincoln featured heavily in the news throughout much of the Iran war, given its deployment lasted a whopping 321 days , 286 of which were without a port call - before it finally returned home to San Diego in early October. The dire conditions aboard the carrier, amid strained logistics and supply lines , caught the attention of Congress - as did stories of deteriorating mental health among some crew members. At a moment Trump administration officials are still hesitant to call it a "war" - the US Navy has confirmed it is extending destroyer deployments from six to at least 11 months , in order to maintain the naval blockade of Iran. This is according to Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, who recently told military families of the extension that at least 17 destroyers are needed for the mission .  "We’ll do our best to bring them home as soon as possible. The problem is the enemy has a vote and they're trying to sink as many ships as possible ," Cao conceded. articles.title: A Heated Hold: FOMC Minutes To Show The Hawks Were Closer To Winning Than The 10-2 Vote Suggested
articles.description: A Heated Hold: FOMC Minutes To Show The Hawks Were Closer To Winning Than The 10-2 Vote Suggested At 2pm today the Fed releases the minutes of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting, and if there is one thing everyone agrees on it's that they won't matter very much. Recall that three weeks ago the Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote , with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of an immediate 25bp hike. It was Cook's first dissent since joining the board in 2022 and, per Fortune, the first time a governor and a regional Fed president dissented on the same side since October 1992 . The statement also upgraded the economy to "strong" from "solid" and promised that the "accumulation of more information" would guide the next move. Translation: we're hiking in December, we just didn't want to do it a week before the midterms (a point several strategists made out loud at the time). Or, as we put it the day after, the hawks lost a vote rather than an argument . articles.description: Why Iraq Just Fast-Tracked Chevron's Takeover Of A 14-Billion-Barrel Supergiant Authored by Simon Watkins via OilPrice.com , U.S. supermajor Chevron has moved from open-ended negotiations under its previous USD200 million exclusivity window to finalizing commercial terms for Iraq's supergiant West Qurna 2 oilfield . Whilst the American firm originally had until February 2027 to use its one-year exclusivity window, following a very recent meeting between Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and Chevron's vice president of business development Joe Cook, the two sides confirmed that contract terms for West Qurna 2 have now been agreed . As it stands, they expect a formal signing of the landmark deal for the huge oilfield before December 31 this year - two months ahead of the expiry of Chevron's exclusive negotiating window. So, why has the deal moved so fast now, and what makes it so special? articles.title: Pentagon Flunks Financial Audit For Ninth Straight Year
articles.description: Pentagon Flunks Financial Audit For Ninth Straight Year Authored by AG News Staff via American Greatness , The Pentagon has failed its financial audit for the ninth fiscal year in a row , the Department of War's Office of Inspector General announced Monday , citing outdated and inadequate financial management systems. The agency-wide audit examined more than $4.8 trillion in assets. About 1,500 auditors from the inspector general's office and independent public accounting firms took part in the review. Investigators found that while the department reported fewer material weaknesses in fiscal 2026, those numbers did not reflect real fixes. Brett Mansfield, the Defense Department's deputy inspector general for audit, said "that reduction stems from consolidation, not resolution." The inspector general's point was that problems had been grouped together, not solved. The inspector general said the components that produce audit reports either kept or improved their opinions in fiscal 2026. Several individual audits remain underway. articles.title: "We Dodged A Bomb": Ex-Con Trainee Indicted Over Device That Emptied 2,500 Homes Around Illinois Ethanol Plant
articles.description: "We Dodged A Bomb": Ex-Con Trainee Indicted Over Device That Emptied 2,500 Homes Around Illinois Ethanol Plant A federal grand jury has indicted a 41-year-old trainee at the Peoria, Illinois, ethanol plant where a bomb was found last Friday , charging him with emailing the company a threat that explosive devices had been placed there. Andrew Kozak of Chillicothe pleaded not guilty to both counts on Tuesday. The threat reached BioUrja Renewables on Friday, Nov. 13, and police found a package at the plant that afternoon. Bomb technicians had it rendered safe by 9:12 p.m., and Police Chief Brad Dixon stressed that it was not a hoax. Peoria police ordered everyone within a mile of the plant to evacuate , including parts of downtown Peoria and East Peoria. Dixon said the order displaced people from an estimated 2,500 homes , and it stayed in place for 18 hours . The FBI has since taken over the case and confirmed the device was a real explosive. The indictment charges Kozak with threats regarding explosives, for threatening to damage and destroy the plant by fire and an explosive, and with interstate communication of a threat. articles.description: Housing Crisis Escalates: Pending Home Sales Hit Record Low, Building Permits Worst Since COVID As Homebuilder Confidence Crashes Update (1000ET) : Following the good (Housing Starts), and bad (Building permits and homebuilder confidence) earlier this morning, we now have the ugly as pending home sales crashed to a record low... NAR reported a 4.69% MoM drop in pending home sales, dragging sales down over 17% YoY... Pending home sales declined across all US regions. The West saw the steepest decline of 6.9%, while sales in the South — the biggest home-selling region — fell 6.3%. The housing crisis is worsening rapidly as mortgage rates hit an almost three-year high in early October before easing somewhat later in the month, but they remain more than a percentage point above pre-war levels. “October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out,” NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun said in a statement.  Hope springs eternal!! articles.title: Small Vessel Trade Thrives in Hormuz As Iran Targets Supertankers
articles.description: Small Vessel Trade Thrives in Hormuz As Iran Targets Supertankers By Tsvetana Paraskova of OilPrice.com Smaller oil tankers moved in October the most volumes of crude oil out of the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, as Iran targets supertankers and incidents with naval mines and unknown projectiles hit a wartime high. The smaller tankers, which can carry less than half the volumes of a supertanker, shipped 2 million barrels per day (bpd) out of the Strait of Hormuz in October, the highest daily volumes since the war began in February, according to Vortexa data cited by Bloomberg . The shipments on Suezmaxes and Aframaxes, mostly via ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, started to materially pick up in September, which coincided with the estimates that overall crude oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded and nearly reached pre-war levels. Gulf producers and oil importers have had to continuously adapt to the changing security and shipping conditions in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
